record.paper_title: Some open problems in computational algebraic geometry
record.original_question: Let k be a field and let phi:k^n -> k^m be a rational map with coordinate functions f_i=p_i(x)/q_i(x) of degrees d_i. Design an efficient algorithm, combining symbolic computation and numerical methods, to determine the degree of phi without relying solely on solving the generic polynomial system p_i(x)-y_i q_i(x)=0 by Groebner-basis computation.

evidence.quote: Let k be a field and φ : k n -> km be a rational map.
Problem 20. Combine the symbolic and numerical methods to design an efficient algorithm for determining the degree of a rational map.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and let $\varphi : k^n \dashrightarrow k^m$ be a rational map whose coordinate functions are $f_i(x) = p_i(x)/q_i(x)$, where $p_i, q_i \in k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ are polynomials of degrees $d_i$ for $i=1,\dots,m$. The degree of $\varphi$ is defined as the cardinality of a generic fibre $\varphi^{-1}(y)$ (equivalently, the degree of the extension of function fields $[k(x_1,\dots,x_n) : k(f_1,\dots,f_m)]$ when $\varphi$ is dominant and generically finite, and $0$ otherwise).

One standard but computationally expensive way to compute $\deg(\varphi)$ is to solve the generic polynomial system
$$p_i(x) - y_i\, q_i(x) = 0, \qquad i = 1,\dots,m,$$
in the variables $x_1,\dots,x_n$ (with $y_1,\dots,y_m$ kept as parameters) by means of a Gröbner-basis computation and to count the number of solutions in a generic fibre.

Design an efficient algorithm, combining symbolic computation and numerical methods (such as homotopy continuation or other techniques of numerical algebraic geometry), that determines $\deg(\varphi)$ from the data $(p_i, q_i)_{i=1}^m$ without relying solely on a Gröbner-basis solution of the above generic system. Establish the correctness of the algorithm and analyze its complexity.
artifact.category_tag: computational algebraic geometry; degree of rational maps
artifact.status_search_result: There has been substantial progress on computing degrees of rational maps via symbolic techniques (e.g., projective-degree algorithms in the Macaulay2 Cremona package; specialization and syzygy-based methods in works such as arXiv:1901.06599 and arXiv:2007.13017) and via numerical algebraic geometry (homotopy continuation as in Bertini and HomotopyContinuation.jl, which can numerically count fibre points). However, no single hybrid symbolic-numerical algorithm is universally recognized as the definitive efficient solution to the problem as posed, so the open-ended algorithmic design problem appears to remain partially addressed rather than fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: projectiveDegrees -- Macaulay2 Cremona package
status_evidence.snippet: Probabilistic algorithm to compute projective degrees of a rational map between projective varieties via saturation of ideals defined on random linear subspaces.
status_evidence.claim: Symbolic probabilistic algorithms exist for projective degrees, which include the degree of the map.

status_evidence.title: Degree of rational maps via specialization
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the degree of a rational map via specialization techniques relating it to syzygies of the base ideal.
status_evidence.claim: Recent symbolic/algebraic advances give effective ways to compute or bound degrees of rational maps.

status_evidence.title: Degree of Rational Maps versus Syzygies
status_evidence.snippet: Upper bounds on the degree of a generically finite rational map between projective varieties expressed via Rees algebra invariants.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical bounds and computational reductions for the degree of a rational map have been developed.
